ultimately it is that calm inner light of intuitive awakening only can destroy bad habits. intuitive awakening means there is not only the conviction but intuitively it can intuit and see the worthlessness of going ahead with this bad habit in future. it can see the future intuitively that “this is not going to help me” so that conviction has to come inside intuitively, then it can be destroyed. the calm inner light of intuitive awakening is represented by Drishtadyumna who was the commander in chief of Pandava army and eventually he is the one who killed Dronacharya (the habit). he could kill Dronacharya because intuitive awakening can only get rid of the habits.
How can we develop that intuitive awakening? Drishtadyumna came out of fire after intense tapas done by his father Drupada. similarly, the awakening comes by spiritual practices; when we do regularly meditation, then that awakening gradually gradually comes—that intuitive awakening through which we can destroy our bad habits.
data.warrior-1-krupacharya-avidyaindividual-d:
the first warrior is Krupacharya, who represents avidya meaning individual delusion. there is some subtle difference between delusion and illusion, which are often used interchangeably. delusion is something universal that affects everyone but illusion is something which affects only particular persons not universal. An example of delusion is “I am this body” because almost everyone thinks that. An example of illusion is if someone has the conviction that it’s impossible to live without taking so many cups of coffee every day. Krupacharya represents that illusion, individual delusion.
The Patanjali Yoga Sutras fifth sutra from chapter 2 reads: “Ignorance is perceiving the non-eternal to be eternal impute to be pure evil to be good what is not soul to be the soul”. that is avidya. by delusion imagination man creates his own illusions of reality and brings them into being. Guruji wrote: “thus man is a miniature creator fashioning good or evil for himself and the phenomenon world of which is an operative part. It is this creative force inherent in man’s thoughts that makes them so formidable. The truth in the adage thoughts or things should be duly respected”.
Guruji goes on saying: “the influence of the force of avidya illusion is such that no matter how ixam the illusion deluded man is loath to part with it”. and Guruji goes on saying very nicely: “man fabricates his own standards of morality and behavior and calls them good irrespective of their disharmony with eternal divine love”.
We have to conquer him because as long as this individual delusion (avidya) is there, we can’t be happy, we can’t be anywhere close to self-realization. Krupacharya survived the war, but that doesn’t mean individual delusion troubles the realized soul. When self-realization happens, the soul’s individuality remains. Soul once it comes out of God it plays many roles incarnation of incarnation but never loses his identity its individuality even after merging with God even after self-realization still that identity is maintained in God in spirit. Kripacharya survived, but he didn’t trouble anymore. we have to conquer that individual delusion.
data.warrior-2-bhishma-egoahamkara#Warrior 2::
next warrior Bhishma, the powerful Bhishma, he stands for ego aham hankar. ego need not be negative. when the soul merely uses the instruments of this body and mind as means to communicate and interact with the world outside, it’s not a problem.
Guruji explained the levels of ego:
“When identified with grass senses and their objects the i-ness becomes the wisdom destroying physical ego”. “When identified with the subtle instruments of perception and knowledge in the astral body the inus becomes a clearer sense of being the astral ego”. “When the ins expresses solely through pure intuitive wisdom the instrument of the causal body it becomes the pure discriminating ego the divine ego”. The Hindu scriptures say: “when this I shall die then will I know who am I”.
Bhishma was killed by Bhishma. he had that gift of inviting his death whenever he wanted (icha marana). the analogy is that my ego wants self-realization, which means dissolving ego, so eventually my ego wants to destroy the ego consciousness. the physical ego and astral ego have to go, then divine ego survives. Bhishma had to go because his defect was that he always wanted all his children, both Kauravas and Pandavas, to live in peace. even when he saw Kauravas erring and troubling Pandavas, he kept quiet and did not punish the guilty. This mirrors our inner life: I want God, but I also want Pandavas (good inclinations like meditation, devotion) and Kauravas (laziness, pride, desires) together. It doesn’t work. Bhishma had to go. the ego has to be subsided.
data.warrior-3-karna-attachmentraga#Warrior 3:
the third warrior Karna, he represents attachment raga. Guruji writes: “Karna signifies the propensity for pursuing material action towards which there is natural attachment because of enjoyment or pleasure derived from it”. Karna represents Patanjali’s raga, which dwells on pleasure. Raga (attachment) and Dwesha (repulsion, represented by Vikarna) are likes and dislikes.
Karna is the principle that causes man to seek work he is attached to because of the pleasure it gives him, and he justifies that action by proclaiming it to be his duty. Karna sided with Duryodhana because he gave him status, but Karna’s overriding desire was to prove that I am superior to Arjuna. his attachment to his own goal was the driving force, not friendship or loyalty to Duryodhana’s welfare.
When Krishna failed in his peace mission and revealed Karna’s identity as the eldest son of Kunti, Karna refused to join the Pandavas, saying it was his duty to protect Duryodhana. He cried, “Why why creator why did you put me in this position?”. He didn’t approach his gurus (Parshuram or Vyasa) for advice because he was afraid of counsel that may go against his attachment to his desire to prove superiority over Arjuna. This overwhelming attachment to his goal eventually brought his downfall and that of his friend Duryodhan and many others.
data.warrior-4-vikarna-repulsiondwesha#Warrio:
next Vikarna represents repulsion dwesha. Guruji wrote: “Vikarna means one who behaves according to his natural tendency in avoiding actions that do not give pleasure that are disagreeable”.
Man’s ignorance creates the dual opposites of likes and dislikes (ragadvesa). Guruji writes: “He is attached to what he likes and avoids what he dislikes rather than exercising discriminative free choice and following what is truly right and best for him”.
A simple example is neglecting essential actions like walking for health because it doesn’t give immediate joy or pleasure—that is repulsion. The story of the saint and the graveyard illustrates this: if a person does not have one hour to walk in the graveyard now, he will soon spend all his time there. The saint added, “and all those who are resting there in the graveyard said the same thing when they were alive I don’t have the time”. We must not allow Vikarna to dominate us. The world conditions us to have likes and dislikes (Karna/Vikarna). For instance, a person who enjoys a football game merely for the skills, without supporting either denominationally aligned team, is sometimes seen as an atheist because the world expects you to have some like some belonging some dislike you should have it.
data.warrior-5-jayadratha-body-bound-inclinat: next Jayadratha represents body bound inclination abhinivesa. Jayadratha represents the subtle tenacity to body attachment, Patanjali’s fifth klesha (trouble). Western psychologists call it the force of self-preservation and noted that it is strongest urge in man. While taking care of the body is permitted, this inclination leads to negative side effects. it expresses itself as fear of death but also gives rise to mortal characteristics contrary to the immortal nature of the true self. These characteristics include selfishness, possessiveness, the storing up of treasures on earth as though this will be his permanent home. Jayadratha was eventually killed by Arjun. Warrior 6: Somadatta’s Son (Material Action/Bhurisrivas) next, the son of Somadatta, also named Bhurisrivas, represents material action. material action that produces binding effects because it is instigated by egoistic desire must be conquered. Guruji writes: “a material action no which produces binding effects that is to be avoided”. The works of a yogi who is established in self-realization leaves no impressions either good or evil to bind him. Actions should be performed with the thought of God so that they do not bind us. The analogy is given of writing on sand (effects left behind, binding) versus writing on water (effects gone, non-binding).
data.warrior-7-dronacharya-habitsamskara#Warr: next warrior is Dronacharya, he represents habit samskara inner tendency. Patanjali’s vipaka. Drona represents samskara—the impressions made on the consciousness by past thoughts and actions which create strong tendencies to repeat themselves. Dronacharya was also a guru of Pandavas; we must remember that habit can also be good.
data.warrior-8-aswatthama-latent-desireashaya:
the last warrior mentioned is Aswatthama, who represents asia of patanjali meaning latent desire. Yogananda writes that “that which remains unchanged and doesn’t perish with death is desire”. More specifically, it is latent desire or desired seed (vasana).
Latent desire (Aswatthama) should be distinguished from active desire (Duryodhana). Active desire is an impulse of the mind that produces an independent wish, and can be checked or suppressed by a quick act of will and wisdom. However, every unfulfilled active desire, unless roasted by wisdom, plants a new desired seed in the mind. These desire seeds are more compelling than the impulsive fresh desires deeply rooting themselves in the subconscious ready to spring up suddenly with demands that are most often unreasonable frustrating and sorrow producing.
Latent desire is frustrating because it springs up suddenly without cause, is compelling, and neither control nor fulfillment is possible. Aswatthama survived the war. The key is to roast that latent desire by wisdom. The example of the boy desiring a toy car shows how wisdom eventually destroyed that latent desire and it no longer bothered him.
Aswatthama did not die, but after committing the terrible act of killing the sons of Draupadi, Krishna made him powerless and allowed him to roam around powerless and friendless all alone. similarly the latent desire may be there inside me but that won’t bother me when I roast it, when I make it powerless by my wisdom.

Now, we will study the SLOKA nine. First, let’s listen to this SLOKA sung by SWAMI VASUDEVANANDAJI: anye ca bahvah sura madarthe tyaktajivitah nanasastrapraharanah sarve yuddhavisaradah anye ca bahvah sura madarthe tyaktajivitah nanasastrapraharanah sarve yuddhavisaradah
The plain meaning as given by GURUDEVA PARAMAHANSAJI, DURYODHANA continues: “And numerous other warriors, all well-trained for battle and armed with various weapons, are here present, ready for my sake to lay down their lives.”. Recall that DURYODHANA first explained the warriors ready to fight for PANDAVAS and then in SLOKAS seven and eight, he narrated the list of warriors ready to fight for him. And he continues here. Those eight warriors we saw last time — like KARNA, VIKARNA, BHISHMA, DRONA, SOMADATTI, ASHVATTHAMAN, DRONA, like that we have seen. Now, he says there are more.
And here GURUJI’s words — very, very informative. GURUJI wrote, “Here is introduced a specialized grouping of KAURAVA forces. Lest the reader feel perplexed at another ‘list,’ he should rather let his thought processes merge with those of the RISHIS, ancient and modern, who realized that yoga is a science demanding exactitude in definition.”. Here, we are trying to understand the life of a YOGI, that is you and me. Life of a YOGI with a mission. You have a mission; I have a mission — that’s Self-realization. Also, to live a life free from pain and suffering and to live in that perpetual joy. It is possible for a YOGI, it is possible, because yoga is a science of how the soul descended from Spirit into this flesh and identified with this body and its environment and the objects, and how it can reascend to Spirit. That is the science of yoga, descending and ascending. Now, we are in the phase of ascending. And this list consists of six persons, SHAT RIPUS. SHAT RIPUS meaning six enemies. When the ego has sided with the materialistic force of creation, it is said to have six faults. What are they? KAMA, KRODHA, LOBHA, MOHA, MADA, MATSARYA. KAMA means lust, desire. KRODHA — anger, LOBHA — greed, MOHA — delusion, temptation. And then MADA — pride, MATSARYA — jealousy. I mean, these are the six enemies we have to fight within. And this desire, anger, greed, temptation, pride, and jealousy are very easy for us to see in others. Sometimes very difficult to see within.

data.detailed-analysis-of-the-shat-ripus#Deta:
No? That’s why we need to study their characteristics — how sometimes they are in disguise inside.
KAMA (Lust/Desire) - Represented by DURYODHANA First let us take KAMA — lust — represented by DURYODHANA. GURUJI wrote, “In the name and guise of fulfilling one’s needs, ego lures man to continuous seeking of self-satisfaction, resulting in suffering and vexation. What would content the soul is forgotten, and the ego goes on endlessly trying to satisfy its insatiable desires.”. Mark these words. How much it applies to each one of us. What would satisfy the ego? What would satisfy the soul is forgotten and the ego starts gratifying desires, again and again, endlessly. So, what satisfies the soul is forgotten. I mean, that’s why all the problems. And these coercive materialistic desires, they’re the instigator of man’s wrong thoughts and actions. It’s not a simple desire having inside. This desire will drive the man into wrong thoughts and wrong actions. I mean, that is the problem. The perfect exemplar is DURYODHANA. And those of us who know the story of MAHABHARATA well, understand this — how DURYODHANA represents the “desire, lust”.
And GURUJI wrote about this. He said, “Lust applies to the abuse of any or all the senses in the pursuit of pleasure or gratification. Through the sense of sight man may lust after material objects.”. Easy to understand. It is sight that sees something and desire starts. It could be a beautiful house, a car, dress, or whatever it is; something we see and eye brings some information and starts a desire. “Through the sense of sight man may lust after material objects; through the sense of hearing, he craves the sweet, slow poison of flattery, and voices and music that rouse his material nature.”. We all want to listen some good things about ourselves. No? Flattery — so, so, so sweet, flattering. “Through the lustful pleasure of smell he’s enticed toward wrong environments and actions; lust for food and drink causes him to please his taste at the expense of health.”. We all understand that. “Through the sense of touch he lusts after inordinate physical comfort and abuses the creative sex impulse.”.
GURUJI goes on, “Lust also seeks gratification in wealth, status, power, dominion — all that satisfies the ‘I, me, mine’ in the egotistical man.”. “I, me, mine!”. No? This is mine. I’m greater! Like that. “I, me and mine” so strong in the egoistic man. “Lust destroys one’s happiness, health, brainpower, clarity of thought, memory, and discriminative judgment.”. So, this strong desire, lust — KAMA — has to be destroyed if you are to have a life free from pain and suffering and Self-realization. And DURYODHANA’S life is full of this — desire, desire for kingdom. Not only the desire for having control over kingdom, he also has a desire to suppress people he didn’t like. PANDAVAS should not exist or they should exist as slaves. That desire so strong, so strong! That is the cause of the war — that strongly egoistical desire. And he won’t even know sometimes.
I have a short story. One boy — maybe about ten. He had a pet — a turtle. He used to take care of it. He would spend a lot of time with the turtle. One day he saw the turtle — motionless. He tapped, no response. It’s dead! He was heartbroken. Heartbroken! No one could console him. Other people were offering other pets — this, that. Nothing would work! He was inconsolably weeping, weeping, weeping, crying, crying! Then his father got an idea and offered something. “KUMAR, whatever happened, happened! Now let us make a big event of this funeral. We will bring a big cart — decorated cart — and we’ll have a music band and we’ll carry this to seashore and bury there. And we’ll do that, all this, and you are there at the head of the procession and everyone would understand that it’s you!”.
And this boy’s face lit up, “Oh, procession, decorated cart and my, my turtle! Oh, that is being honoured; that means I’m being honoured. We’re going in a procession. Everyone is going to watch.”. He said, “Yes, let’s do it.”. See, he reconciled immediately. Cart was brought, well decorated, music party was there ready, and they went to bring this turtle. When they went there, turtle started moving, playing. You know, that means it didn’t really die. It just, it was completely still at that time. When it started moving, this boy was so upset. “Everything is ready! Kill it! First kill it, then you can carry. We can carry to seashore. Kill it!”. Now you see what was in boy’s mind. Was it love for turtle? Or the thrill that comes out of love for the turtle? All along he thought that he was loving turtle. No! If it was real love this thought even doesn’t come. When he saw turtle moving, he would have been very happy. But he was more interested in all this HUNGAMA outside. And that he is going to miss, so kill it. That is the desire. Desire for sense gratification. Desire to please the mind. Not exactly this is genuine desire. DURYODHANA did that again and again. For instance, at least he thought he was a good friend of KARNA. KARNA became his friend because he wanted some protection. DURYODHANA, he could see the potential in KARNA who could stand up to ARJUNA. No one else could in his clan. So, here is a possibility to stand ARJUNA. So, he made a king instantaneously without knowing who KARNA was. Instantaneously, in the very first meeting, he made him a king so he would help him, and that was not love for him so much. It was love for his own desire. And KARNA, also, without knowing anything about DURYODHANA, accepted it because that was going to satisfy his attachment — desire to prove that he was superior to ARJUNA. So, it was a mutual arrangement like that, not the love.
And recall the incident of GHATOTKACHA. During the war, GHATOTKACHA, the son of BHIMA, he was going berserk. He was killing so many people and no one could face him. That time, DURYODHANA requested KARNA, “Now, use your ASTRA, the missile, which you got from DEVDENDRA, and kill him.”. Then KARNA replies, “No, I have saved this particular ASTRA — missile, to use it against ARJUNA, who is the most powerful on the other side.”. Then DURYODHANA, instantaneously, said that, “No, this is the need of the hour now. If you don’t do it our friendship is not going to be any more — that will end. Our friendship will end.”. He threatened him, and he knows very well if KARNA used this ASTRA against GHATOTKACHA, KARNA would be vulnerable. He is losing his powers, vulnerable. But that was not the interest of DURYODHANA. Immediately he had to solve this problem. He could have used many other tricks. ASHVATTHAMAN was there with so many weapons; DRONACHARYA was there, so many weapons. But no! Here, I mean that is the desire and even when he thinks that’s love, the background is the desire to satisfy his own.
KRODHA (Anger) - Represented by DUHSHASANA Next. Next quality KRODHA — anger. Anger is represented by DUHSHASANA. The very name itself, DUH-SHASANA — “duh” means hard, “shasana” means control. Hard to control! That is anger. In second chapter, 63rd SLOKA, BHAGAVAN KRISHNA says, “Anger causes the wrongdoer to be enveloped in delusion, which then obscures memory of the correct behaviour of the Self, causing decay of the discriminative faculty. From this confusion of intelligence, annihilation of right behaviour follows.”. I mean, it’s a degradation. It all starts from anger. In anger, it’s possible we don’t know what we are doing, what we are speaking. That means, temporarily, we are enveloped in delusion. Loss of memory of right behaviour and discriminative faculty — like that, it’s so dangerous. “Even if anger is supposedly justified, so-called ‘righteous anger,’ it must never take the place of calm, discriminative judgement and action.”. Sometimes we have to display anger — I would say “display” — I mean, with our children just to put them to right course of action. Or sometimes with our juniors, we may have to “display” some anger. You know, it’s just a “display.”. Here I give an example: Once GURUJI was unhappy with one devotee. He was giving instructions, you know, and that devotee was standing there in a corridor, at the end of the corridor. GURUJI was walking towards him making a face and saying, “No, no!” this, that, etc. His face was red. GURUJI’s face was red, like full of anger, you know. Very clear, angry! GURUJI was not happy what has happened. So, he was giving instruction, and after walking towards him, and then he returned, he turned and returned, going other direction full of smiles. Devotees standing this side, they could see only full of smile. That means even while he was displaying his anger; he was fully in control of his emotions and that anger he was displaying with one purpose. So that, that person realizes the gravity of the situation: “I angered GURUDEVA, I will not do this again.”. To send that message that something wrong has happened, you realize it, acknowledge it. So, that’s why he displayed that anger, but completely in control of his emotions. Instantaneously he turns and smiles. I mean, that is “righteous anger.”. I mean, sometimes it is required when we are dealing with children or juniors, etc. But not at the cost of that discrimination. And we should have control on emotions. That second warrior we have to face – KRODHA.
LOBHA (Greed) - Represented by KARNA and VIKARNA Next is LOBHA. LOBHA is greed. GURUJI writes: “From childhood, most persons are conditioned to be governed by their ego, and hence led by their feelings and guided by scheduled likes and dislikes. This enslavement to whims, likes and dislikes, is LOBHA — greed.”. And here we have to understand why likes and dislikes lead to greed. And greed is represented by KARNA and VIKARNA. Both together represent greed. We know KARNA represents attachment — likes. VIKARNA represents repulsion — dislike. Together they represent LOBHA. I mean, how likes and dislikes, attachment and repulsion, lead to greed? I would like to give one example. Say wealth. We quite often we see people having greed for wealth. How is it coming from likes and dislikes? Because there is a push-pull effect. It’s push-pull effect. See, I want wealth, it is almost natural because I have that attachment — like for comforts in life, luxuries, status, fame etc. All these things can come from wealth, you know. My luxuries, comforts, name, status, all this come from wealth, if I have. So, these comforts, and luxuries etc. my attachment to these pull me towards that wealth. These attachments are pulling me towards wealth. At the same time, I have dislike — repulsion towards simplicity, poverty you know, living a low-profile life in the society. I have repulsion to this, and this repulsion here pushes me towards acquiring wealth. So, the dislikes here, dislike for simplicity, poverty, etc, they push me towards wealth, and the attraction towards comforts and fame and name and status pull me towards acquiring wealth. The net effect is greed for wealth, more and more and more. So, this push-pull effect — likes and dislikes — push us towards that greed for whatever that object may be.
What is greed? “Greed is acquisitiveness, possessing more and more, a confusion of mind between necessary necessities and unnecessary necessities.”. This is something which GURUJI coined — “Necessary necessities and unnecessary necessities”. They are originally unnecessary, but as we go along, they become so much necessary. Mind cannot distinguish. Is it really required? I mean, that’s coming from greed. Once we are in that mood of greed, we don’t understand. For example, one common form of greed is for food. Sometimes I go on taking food, although my body doesn’t need any more. I am taking a little more, little more food only to satisfy my tongue, taste buds. Instant gratification I need, forgetting the impact of taking that extra food, or sometimes even wrong food, forgetting the impact it’s going to have on my health. That is greed. Greed for food. Not that what is required, but I, whether it is necessary or unnecessary, I don’t even distinguish.
“Greed leads to stealing, dishonesty, cheating, self-surfeit at the expense of the well-being of others.”. We see this so much in the world. No? Is not the greed which leads to stealing, which leads to dishonesty? That’s it. That greed can, you know, sometimes a person may ask, say maybe ten rupees or hundred rupees, maybe because he in need of money, you know? Of course, we don’t have to give him. It’s not correct way, but still you know, ten rupees — ok, it’s alright. But sometimes people demand ten LAKH, a million rupees, that’s not out of need, it’s out of, completely, greed. Look at dishonesty coming into picture because of greed — greed for money. And in sixteenth chapter of BHAGAVAD GITA, “BHAGAVAN KRISHNA warns the devotee ARJUNA the threefold gate to hell is lust, anger and greed; therefore, these must be abandoned.”. Lust, anger and greed, most dangerous enemies out of the six enemies. That is DURYODHANA, DUHSHASANA, KARNA, VIKARNA. Even KURUKSHETRA, we know that these are formidable enemies — DURYODHANA, DUHSHASANA, KARNA, VIKARNA. We have to conquer them.
I have one incident — this is a real-life incident I would like to share. Way back in 1983, I was teaching a course at CONCORDIA University, MONTREAL, CANADA. I finished my course and then conducted an examination. After the exam, one student approached me. You know, he pleaded, “Sir, I did not do exam well. If I fail, I’ll be thrown out of the course, I’m already on probation. Last two years I have been, and this a particular test I’m taking the third time, this subject. If I fail once again, I’ll be thrown out of the course and two years study will be wasted. I’m on probation sir, please give me a passing grade.” That’s ‘C’ — ’A, B, C, D,’ we have grading system there. “C grade, you please give me. I didn’t do well.”. I said, “I have not yet evaluated the scripts, let me see.”. Afterwards, when I was evaluating the answer scripts, this particular man did very bad. Very bad. He deserved only a ‘D’ that mean fail, but I remembered his face clearly, so what I did is, I just added one mark here, two marks there, somehow pushed him to ‘C’. Somehow, you know? Ok, it’s ok. ‘C’. And I forgot about it. A couple of days later, he again came back to me “Sir, what happened to my exam?”. Then I thought of giving self-confidence to him to boost his morale. I said, “You did fairly well. On his own you got grade ‘C.’. I didn’t have to do anything. You got on your own grade ‘C’.”. I wanted to, you know, give a boost to his self-confidence so that he would do better later. “You did well — ‘C’.”. He was surprised. “’C’, SWAMIJI, sir — I got ‘C’?”. “Yes.”. Then he said, “Sir, can you make it ‘B’?”. Immediately he was, “Can you make it ‘B’?”. This time I was shocked. He knew very well that he didn’t even deserve ‘C’ — somehow, he got it. That was a need — ‘C’ was need. But ‘B’ was greed. “Can you give me ‘B’?” — immediately! I mean, that is greed, that is greed. We should always go by our needs, what we need, and also what we deserve. If we forget these two things, in daily life also, in daily life, greed sets in and with greed comes so many other problems, so many other problems — dishonesty, this and that comparisons — so many things can come. So let’s be watchful.
MOHA (Delusion/Temptation) - Represented by SHAKUNI Next – MOHA. That is delusion, of course, represented by SHAKUNI. We know SHAKUNI was the maternal uncle of the KAURAVAS — DURYODHAN, DUSHASAN, VIKARNA — all those hundred brothers. He was their mother’s brother, maternal. PARAMAHANSA YOGANANDAJI said: “…MOHA is represented by SHAKUNI noted for winning battles through deceptive bewilderment of his opponents.”. “When the symbology of the characters is understood, the meaning of the allegory cannot be missed.”.
And we know the part played by SHAKUNI in MAHABHARATA. In a way, he was the root cause because by deceptive means, he played that game of dice, and PANDAVAS lost everything they had. That he’s the one — he was not straightforward, he was not honest by all — you know deceiving them in the game of dice, he threw them out. And that is temptation — a form of delusion, of course. YUDHISTHIRA yielded to temptation, isn’t it true? That’s how he went into the game of dice, it was tempting and he lost. Now tell me who killed SHAKUNI? Who overpowered SHAKUNI eventually? It was not ARJUNA or BHIMA. SHAKUNI was killed by SAHADEVA — the youngest of the PANDAVAS. SAHADEVA represents YAMA. YAMA means the power to resist — you know power to resist evil, that is YAMA. NIYAMA is the power to follow the good path — NIYAMAS. YAMA is the power to resist. So, eventually temptation was conquered by the power to resist, I mean very true, very clear here.
That is why GURUJI advised that if we don’t have the willpower, develop won’t power. Won’t power. The won’t power is the power to resist and that is one which can take us away from temptation. It’s like this. Suppose something is happening. It’s a very tempting situation. There is very tempting situation. If we say, “It’s alright, I have enough willpower, I can still be around.”. We don’t know when our willpower will be lost, self-control will be lost. In that, if we don’t have full self-control, best is say, “I won’t.”. Get out of the situation. Later you can figure out. When calmness returns, when you are in a better, peaceful environment, you could think about it — pros and cons of the particular activity, or whatever. If you are still there in that environment where there is so much temptation and sometimes very difficult to conquer, we may fall prey. We may fall prey. So let us develop at least won’t power. Eventually that YAMA was the one who conquered the temptation — SHAKUNI. You know many addicts — those who are addicted to you know, various substances — they said the same thing initially. “I will not be an addict. I have the willpower; I am just trying this for fun. Just fun for once or twice. I’m just trying this.”. And we don’t know where it leads to. Everyone tried only for fun in the beginning — all this, all the addictive substances. If only that person had that won’t power. “No, I don’t need to try this.”. Won’t power! Get out of the situation. Get out of the environment. That is what we have to do. There is another advice which says that “Don’t tempt temptation to tempt you.”. Don’t tempt temptation to tempt you — it could be anything, addiction, it could be some other action, it could be food or it could be anything, any of the senses. It could happen even with the TV, “Oh, just ten minutes I’ll sit there.”. Very tempting. That ten minutes could be an hour and a half. Tempting! So best is willpower. If you don’t have willpower, at least won’t power; come out. So we have to be constantly on the guard, if we are to be happy in this life. Discrimination is required.
MADA (Pride) - Represented by SHALYA Next, MADA — meaning pride. Pride is represented by SHALYA. SHALYA was the maternal uncle of NAKULA, SAHADEVA. And maternal uncle of even all PANDAVAS in a way because NAKULA, SAHADEVA’S mother was MADRI, whose brother was SHALYA. GURUJI wrote, “Pride here means that love for the ‘I’, or ego-self, that is constantly on the defensive (or offensive) to support and promote the interests of self.”. When all the time it’s “me, me, I am superior” — that pride. Again, sometimes it could be very subtle, you know, very subtle. “Because of pride, within the ego there arises arrogance, conceit, haughtiness, wanton lust after the desires, interests, or demands of the ‘I, me, and mine.’ ”. Isn’t it true? “I am superior. Me. People come to me because I am greater. Mine. My house is better. I, me and mine” so strong in the egoistic man. SHALYA was maternal uncle of PANDAVAS, and he started from his kingdom — MADRA kingdom — to join PANDAVAS in the KURUKSHETRA war — to help PANDAVAS he started. But on the way, DURYODHANA played tricks and bribed him with gifts and flattery and eventually turned him against PANDAVAS and enlisted him in his support. I mean, this is what can happen if there is pride in man. GURUJI says, “Thus does egoistic pride often turn man’s head — and feet — in the wrong direction.”. This man, SHALYA, with good intention he started to help PANDAVAS, but he turned in the wrong direction, and went to KAURAVAS, because of the pride. “Pride makes the egotistical man, consciously or unconsciously, try to cut off the heads of others to make himself appear taller. It likes to belittle or humiliate others, to gloat on their mistakes and discomfiture and to gossip and criticize.”. I mean, yes, pride is that one is, “I am better. I am superior. I am richer, I am this, I am that, I am more powerful; I am more skillful.”. At the same time, “That person is weaker. That person is worse; he is inferior to me.”. I mean, that is also there, both: “I am better” and “he is worse.”. And you can always see something in others to criticize — gossip — everything coming from pride. And GURUJI warns even spiritual people may fall. May fall. From a great position of advancement, they may fall if pride is there. “The greater the good in man, the more there is to be proud about, increases the chance of succumbing to egoistic pride. Cunning, indeed, are the traps of delusion.”. Cunning indeed are traps of delusion. I mean, if I am a better person there’s a greater possibility of being proud. So, watch out. Watch out. If there is pride, there cannot be God and God’s mercy. God’s mercy — GURUJI said that, you know — it is collected in the valleys of humility, not on the mountaintops of pride. Water gets collected only in the valleys, not on the mountaintop. This is pride. That is humility.
Now. SHALYA — let’s go to KURUKSHETRA war. In the initial days of KURUKSHETRA war SHALYA killed UTTARA KUMAR. UTTARA KUMAR was the son of VIRATA. VIRATA represents SAMADHI. Offspring of SAMADHI is joy, is joy. When you meditate, you go into that SAMADHI state and there you will feel that joy in meditation, and that is the offspring of SAMADHI — VIRATA. But SHALYA killed him because if there is pride, there’s no joy. Pride can kill the result of your good meditation, too. If you are very proud, that affects the result of your meditation. That joy is gone. Pride kills the joy as SHALYA killed the son of VIRATA. Now. Can you tell me who killed SHALYA — eventually SHALYA was killed — but who killed? YUDHISTHIRA. YUDHISTHIRA killed SHALYA. YUDHISTHIRA represents that calmness, born of stillness and the deep silence, that calmness — he killed pride. Because in that stillness within, in that calmness there is no room for pride.
And I would like to read out something GURUJI wrote in Metaphysical Meditations about: here PARAMAHANSAJI is writing about silence. He said, “My silence, like an expanding sphere, spreads everywhere. My silence spreads like a wildfire of bliss; the dark thickets of sorrow and the tall oaks of pride are all burning up.”. See my silence means that deep silence; GURUJI is talking about the deep silence, not just silence of mere silence of vocal cords. That is much deeper. Thoughts have to be silent, emotions have to be silent. All senses have to be silent. That is the deeper silence GURUJI is talking about — the stillness, calmness. It spreads like a wildfire of bliss and it burns the thickets of sorrow and tall oaks of pride, all burning up, because in that it very easy to visualize this — feel. Those of us who meditate can feel that when there is joy of meditation, that joy comes with a sense of gratitude, not with a sense of pride, “I’m having joy.”. No, you are so grateful. You are so humble. It comes with that sense of gratitude, and there’s no room for pride; it’s gone. Even if we have pride otherwise during the day, at the end of meditation you are enjoying that calmness. There is no pride. And this understanding that I’m a part of God, I’m a part of SAT-CHIT-ANANDA, — ANANDA, that joy — it comes with a sense of humility, not that “I am God” or “I am powerful.”. No! It comes with understanding that everything is God, including this little self. It’s God that’s manifesting everywhere. I mean, it comes with a sense of gratitude and humility, not that “I have now knowledge. I have gained spiritual knowledge.”. It doesn’t go well. It doesn’t last long. So, pride can never be the quality of a spiritual person.
That has to be, and that may be there you know? Sometimes when you see people, we may be may be thinking that they’re not all that spiritual — you know that pride: “I am more spiritual. I spend more time in spiritual pursuits, meditational practices. Whereas, they are spending time, wasting their time.”. That is pride. That is pride. Have understanding. Have understanding. Never have pride in your achievements and in your actions, I mean that doesn’t go with the spiritual life. Very simple. Very simple. Pride. I have a short story. There was one very rich person, very rich, very comfortable. All his life, he was very comfortable. Made a name, and towards the end he was bedridden. He thought that his end is nearing and introspected. And thought that, “Okay, material achievements were there, but I never prayed. I never gave attention to God, religion. I think this is the time now I should start praying; make acquaintance with God.”. You know, very sincere desire. That understanding dawned on him. Then he felt that, “I don’t know how to pray. I don’t know how to involve in any spiritual practices, but I know my servant PRABHAKAR, he’s very good at it. I see him regularly spending time in PUJAS, worship, this and praying. I’ll ask his advice. So, he asked PRABHAKAR, “I’m almost at the end of my life, I want to pray. Please teach me how to pray, how to worship.”. He said, “Master, it’s very simple. Please go to your cowshed — GOSHALA. There bend on your knees, and with folded hands and bent head sincerely say, ‘Lord, I surrender to you.’ ”. This man said, “What? I have to go to cowshed, GOSHALA. There kneel in mud and stinking place; I cannot go. Even if I did, what would my neighbours think? They’re all seeing, watching me there kneeling in mud, in GOSHALA for praying. Impossible! I can’t do it. I can’t do it. No, no, this is not the way.”. He just rejected the offer. PRABHAKAR said, “As you wish,” and went away.
And this man continued his thinking. After a couple of months, he thought, “What? There is still no peace of mind for me. Maybe I have to do that. I have to go to cowshed, there I have to kneel. Probably that is the only way to approach God.”. Then he called for PRABHAKAR and said, “PRABHAKAR, please take me to cowshed. I’m ready to kneel in mud and pray.”. Then PRABHAKAR said, “Master, not necessary. Your willingness to go there to cowshed and kneel there in mud, your willingness to do that, that is enough. God would be very pleased; you can pray right here. You bend here and do right here.”. I mean that’s what he said, that willingness — all along it’s pride: “I have a status. I cannot do this. What would the neighbours think?”. I mean that’s pride — it was all in mind. When he cleared that in mind, “I’m just a child of God as anyone else.”. There’s nothing like superior or inferior, especially when it comes to praying. When he understood that, it was really not required to go there. I mean this is understanding he had to receive, not to go to cowshed or not. That willingness, willingness is important. This came after he conquered pride. He conquered his pride — that willingness was there and the result was there. Freedom — freedom from that chain of pride.
You know, it was holding him. Let us also understand, when we have to be proud, if at all. Sometimes we are very proud of the achievement of children, achievement of our nation. That’s fine, that’s a positive thing actually. It’s not like being proud in God’s eyes, no. But I would like to warn you of something — that willingness to go there was adequate, he was told. It doesn’t mean that willingness to meditate is adequate. There you have to sit down and meditate. Willingness to go there, all the way there, that was willingness. Not that, “I have willingness to meditate, but I can’t meditate.”. That doesn’t work that way.
MATSARYA (Jealousy) - Represented by KRITAVARMA Next, the sixth enemy, MATSARYA — jealousy, represented by KRITAVARMA. KRITAVARMA was a YADAVA king who fought for DURYODHANA against PANDAVAS, because the bride he wanted to marry was taken to the kingdom of KRISHNA and married to KRISHNA, so he was jealous of KRISHNA. He was jealous of KRISHNA and eventually he landed up fighting against KRISHNA for KAURAVAS.
GURUJI wrote: “MATSARYA, or ego envy, in its full implication, incites the lust of desire. It makes one forget his true duty, those actions that are correct for his own soul evolution, and creates in him longings to imitate the position of others — that he might be or have what has aroused envy in him.”. We can understand jealousy; we also go through that, thoughts of jealousy, but if it’s just for an instant the thought of jealousy comes, it’s fine — you’ve conquered it. But if you harbour it, harbour it, then it becomes a very negative force inside. And your behaviour won’t be normal, especially toward that particular person about whom you are envy about, or with others also, your behaviour is not normal. Because of circumstances sometimes a thought may come, but conquer it immediately: “No, it’s not wise.”. See KRITAVARMA was one of the three KAURAVA warriors who survived. He was not killed. KRIPACHARYA, ASHVATTHAMAN and KRITAVARMA. Does it mean that even after Self-realization jealousy is going to be there? No, you have to understand it in the right perspective. What is jealousy? I am jealous of someone when that someone has something which I want and I don’t have. Then only am I jealous of him. I’m not jealous of some millionaire because I never think of becoming a millionaire. But I may be jealous of someone who has something which I want, but I don’t have. Then only the jealousy comes. In Self-realization — when one with God — I have everything that I can imagine in this creation. I have everything — one with God, that love, joy, wisdom. Everything I have. There is nothing which I don’t have and other person has. So, there is no room for jealousy. It’s just powerless. That quality is there still in the ether, but powerless because I have no thought of having anything which other person has, which I don’t have at this point: I have everything — one with God, I am a Self-realized, nothing here we are missing. So KRITAVARMA, although he didn’t die, it’s all right, he’s not going to disturb us anymore.
So that’s about 6 qualities mentioned in this ninth SLOKA: KAMA, KRODHA, MOHA, LOBHA, MADA, MATSARYA — lust, anger, greed, temptation, jealousy, pride — these six.
data.encouragement-sloka-ten#Encouragement (S: Sometimes it may appear to be overwhelming. Overwhelming. You know, if I analyse dispassionately, there are too many KAURAVA warriors in me; either too many, or sometimes too strong. That particular DUHSHASANA may be too strong in me. The short-temperedness may be there — anger, or some, like that, there are too many, or too strongly. And on the other hand, I may not be fully happy with my PANDAVA soul forces. They are not so strong; they are not so many, but there’s no room for discouragement. No room. And this is very clear in next SLOKA, tenth. I just read out the SLOKA; I don’t go into details. Here, DURYODHANA continues. After explaining PANDAVAS and then KAURAVAS, DURYODHANA tells his guru DRONACHARYA: “These, our forces protected by BHISHMA are unlimited (but may be insufficient); whereas their army, defended by BHIMA, is limited (but quite adequate).”. Meaning, numbers-wise KAURAVAS outnumber PANDAVAS, that so many, and so powerful, I have, limitless, but may be inadequate. And even in the heart of hearts, DURYODHANA also realized that because PANDAVAS are on the righteous side, there, and BHAGAVAN KRISHNA was there. So, same thing with us, there may be too many negative qualities. Doesn’t matter. Because in the divine order, in God’s creation, His wish is that you win and I win. I mean, that’s not only my wish and your wish, our GURU’S wish; it is the wish of God, that’s cosmic design. Eventually, each one of us will be able to conquer the negative tendencies inside and have that lasting happiness and eventually, Self-realization. That is for sure. I mean, that is for sure. It’s just a question of when, not whether. So, that’s why we are involved in this SADHANA — spiritual SADHANA so that we hasten our progress. Because as long as we are not in that spiritual consciousness, as long as we are not progressing spiritually, we are suffering. Whatever disappointments in life we have, these are all the result of that mortal consciousness, rather than divine consciousness. So, let us hasten the process, let’s get serious about it. I have to eliminate this. I have to eliminate these negative tendencies.
data.importance-of-uprooting-ego-consciousnes:
Now, why do we have to study so much about these negative qualities, and sometimes it’s painful to see that there are some traces of these qualities within, sometimes. Why do I have to study these? And GURUJI has explained beautifully at the end of this explanation of ninth SLOKA, he goes into this. GURUJI wrote, “It is necessary to understand and uproot the beginning of ego consciousness and its various tendencies, which preclude familiarity with the true Self.”. I mean, that is the basis. As long as we have these negative inclinations, as long as they come into, you know, come to surface in our life, then we are mortals. We forget about immortal nature because we are in the realm of mortality, this. So, we have to understand them and remove from our consciousness.
And GURUJI gives guidelines how to go about it. “The aspiring YOGI should always bear in mind, when he feels angry, ‘That is not me!’”. When you’re angry, say that’s not me, that’s a KAURAVA to be eliminated. That’s not me. That’s not my true nature — no. “When his self-possession is being overpowered by lust or greed, he should say to himself, ‘That is not me!’”. This is some greed in me. This is some strong lust in me. No, that’s a KAURAVA. “When hatred tries to obscure his real nature with a mask of ugly emotion, he should forcefully dissociate himself from it: ‘That is not me.’”. Hatred — if some hatred comes in my mind against anyone, hatred — no, that’s not me! That’s an enemy. “He learns to shut the doors of his consciousness against all undesirable visitors seeking lodging within.".
And whenever that devotee has been used or abused by others, and yet he feels within a stirring of the holy spirit of forgiveness and love, he can then affirm with conviction, ‘That is me! That is my real nature.’”. When you have that sense of forgiveness, in spite of what he has done, when “it’s okay, let me forgive,” when that forgiveness comes, say “That is me. That is my real nature.”. Whenever you feel some love for others or a sense of service to downtrodden, say, “That is me. That is a PANDAVA in me.”. Recognize it and support and affirm. Cultivate this.
GURUJI ends this ninth SLOKA: “Yoga meditation is the process of cultivating and stabilizing the awareness of one’s real nature, through definite spiritual and psychophysical methods and laws by which the narrow ego is displaced by the consciousness of the soul.”. That is what the entire exercise is all about — to replace the consciousness of ego by soul consciousness. Here we have discussed about various KAURAVA warriors and PANDAVA warriors and what they represent, etc.
There is one warning. The characters are not arbitrarily chosen to represent various psychological traits. They are not arbitrarily chosen — attach anger to this person, attach devotion to this person, etc. No, they were chosen understanding the Sanskrit root meaning of the name of the person and/or the part played by that person in MAHABHARATA. For example, DUHSHASANA. His name itself suggests that it’s anger. “Duh-shasana” — hard to control — anger. DURYODHANA. Now, we have seen what the role he was playing, that desire for control, the desire to oppress other people, that desire — he is King Material Desire, controlling everyone.
The true way to understand a scripture is through intuition, attuning oneself to the inner realization of truth. We should not be misled by enthusiasm and the imaginative habit of trying to squeeze spiritual significance from every word or statement or event. I mean, this is what sometimes we tend to do. So much is happening. They are definitely meaningful — all that is explained in the book — and trying to extract spiritual meaning, you know, squeeze spiritual meaning from every character, every word or incident that happened in MAHABHARATA; that is over-enthusiasm. It’s not needed. It’s intellectual, just little gimmicks, that’s all. What is required is understand, the good inclinations and bad inclinations, and how to support and cultivate the good inclinations so that we have a life free from pain and suffering, leading to lasting happiness. And evil tendencies, realize them. We can relate to KAURAVAS. It’s easy to recognize that way, but not trying to squeeze some meaning out of everything that has happened in MAHABHARATA.
data.the-story-of-the-bitter-gourd-karela#The:
There is one story. After KURUKSHETRA war, PANDAVAS were unhappy with what happened, because war, you know, it was a battle where their own relatives, friends were killed. They were unhappy. They thought of going for a pilgrimage and taking holy dip in many sacred rivers so to wash out their, some of their sins accrued in a battle. It happens always: negative vibrations, to wash out negative vibrations, so they wanted to take holy dip in many rivers and pilgrimages, have DARSHAN. They went to BHAGAVAN KRISHNA and asked him. “We are going on a pilgrimage to wash away our sins, to get rid of these negative vibrations and the discomfort, you know, mental discomfort. Please accompany us.”. KRISHNA said, “No, I cannot go with you, but in my place, I give you this bitter gourd — KARELA — bitter gourd. You take this and in whichever river you are taking bath, this also dip on my behalf. And please bring it back to me.”. PANDAVAS went, river after river, you know, different pilgrim centres they visited all over the country. And everywhere, wherever they were taking bath, they also gave a bath to this bitter gourd, KARELA. They dipped in the holy waters, and they returned.
And when they met BHAGAVAN KRISHNA, he said, “What happened to my bitter gourd? Did you give it a good dip everywhere?”. “Yes, in all rivers. Here is it.”. BHAGAVAN KRISHNA took that and cut into pieces. And he gave one piece to each of the PANDAVAS. He said, “Please taste it.”. They tasted and said, “It’s bitter.”. “What? It’s still bitter? But it took bath in so many sacred rivers. But just taking dip in rivers, bitterness won’t go.”. There lies the solution, the point. Just taking bath in different rivers, your negative vibrations won’t go so easily, just taking bath. You have to go through a process. The bitter gourd has to go through a process to lose its bitterness. Isn’t it true? You have to cook. You have to boil, do something, then bitterness is gone and becomes edible, without that bitterness.
Similarly, if you want to get rid of the negative vibrations, whatever you have accrued with all these negative influences, it’s not just enough to go to places and having sacred dips. It’s very good. That gives us some strength. That gives us some inspiration. But what is more important is go through a process so that you can get rid of these negative tendencies and negative vibrations. That is yoga meditation. That is yoga meditation. There is no escape. You do whatever, something, if not yoga meditation, some other technique, some other PUJA, some other worship, something. This is where we actual involving, involving Self. It is not externally doing something that can get rid of it. The external things will help us to inspire, to inspire, but that’s not adequate.
We have to do that. And you and I are fortunate. We are really fortunate because we know what to do, having come to the feet of a SATGURU, PARAMAHANSA YOGANANDAJI. He has given us, for instance, apart from scientific meditations, he also given us many other techniques, like affirmations, visualizations, devotional songs, COSMIC CHANTS; so many things he has given us. By following these, practising them, we get rid of the negative tendencies, negative vibrations, and we progress. So, we are fortunate, we are fortunate.

Love and greetings from the depth of my heart to all of you. Welcome to today’s discourse, which is the fifth in the series of talks on the wisdom of BHAGAVAD GITA, as interpreted by PARAMAHANSA YOGANANDAJI in his book “God Talks With ARJUNA”. Just to quickly review what we have discussed in the last four discourses. We’re all convinced that we are all different expressions of the same Divinity. I am a spark of God, as you are. But I lost the divine kingdom in the game of delusion, as PANDAVAS lost their kingdom in the game of dice.
After losing their kingdom, PANDAVAS had to go into exile for 13 years. After serving their term of exile, 13 years, they came back and demanded the kingdom, which belonged to them morally and legally, but KAURAVAS sitting here in HASTINAPUR, denied. Having left with no other option, KAURAVAS declared a war and hence this KURUKSHETRA war. I’m also banished from my divine kingdom, as I’m under the spell of delusion, MAYA. And I’m living as a mere mortal, incarnation after incarnation. I’m just living like this.
But when I realize that my kingdom is within, that is divine kingdom, full of love and joy and wisdom. I want it back. But my mere wanting back my real kingdom is not adequate. Because the KAURAVAS sitting in me — the negative tendencies like ego, jealousy, pride, habits — these are KAURAVAS sitting in me. They are preventing me to get back my kingdom. So, I have to declare a war, the KURUKSHETRA within, to defeat my evil tendencies by my good inclinations. So that is the KURUKSHETRA within, going on all the time. PARAMAHANSA YOGANANDAJI gave one assurance. He wrote, “Each person has to fight his own battle of KURUKSHETRA. It is a war not only worth winning, but in the divine order of the universe and of the eternal relationship between the soul and God, a war that sooner or later must be won.”. So, a war that must be won as per cosmic design, as per God’s wish. It’s just a question of sooner or later. Let it be sooner. Let’s make it sooner. So that is the KURUKSHETRA war we are waging inside. We studied the first SLOKA.
The first SLOKA tells us the fundamental truth that life is a series of battles between ignorance and wisdom, soul and body, discrimination and the senses, self-control and temptation, and the like. It’s always a series of wars going on. And the import of the first SLOKA is that each night every sincere devotee has to introspect and see how his good tendencies and bad tendencies were in the battlefield of life. Like SANJAYA, who represents honest introspection, revealed to DHRITARASHTRA, the blind mind. So, we have to introspect ourselves to know what is happening.
The second SLOKA gives us a warning. The summary reads, “Thus we find the second SLOKA of the GITA forewarning the spiritual aspirant that King DURYODHANA — Material Desire — will try to arouse man’s DRONA sense, habit tendencies, to fight against the soul forces of discrimination.”. Bad habits are inside, so, the warning here is that whenever a devotee realizes the importance of spiritual practices like meditation, that time, the past bad habits try to prevent him because the Material Desire inside gets alarmed. “This person is going now spiritual way. So, I may lose control over this body and may not be satisfied anymore. So discourage him.”. So, it asks past habit, that is DRONACHARYA, to discourage him. That’s why oftentimes when we are about to meditate, then we remember the many important things we have to do at that time. That is DRONACHARYA, past habit, trying to dissuade us. But there is hope, because DRONACHARYA was guru of not only KAURAVAS, he was also guru of PANDAVAS — meaning habit could be bad or it could be even good.
So let us cultivate the good habits and same DRONACHARYA, the same habit, will help us to win this KURUKSHETRA war. In spiritual practices, especially in meditation, that DRONACHARYA is regularity. That’s a habit, good habit. If we cultivate that regularity in our meditations half the battle is won. So, it’s very important.
Next, the third SLOKA explains that, “When Material Desire and his army of sense-tendencies and their restless thoughts try to reinforce themselves by Past Material Habit, in order to dissuade the spiritual aspirant from the practice of meditation, they find that the Calm Inner Light of awakening intuition, well trained in meditation by Past Spiritual Habit, has effectively arrayed the discriminative faculties to give metaphysical resistance.”. It’s very simple to understand this. Every devotee by nature has that inner urge to progress spiritually by regular SADHANA — like every student would like to study regularly in order to have a prosperous career. But unfortunately, the habits of procrastination, laziness, a tendency to have instant sense gratification, oppose the spiritual practices — SADHANA, regular studies by students. But again, there is hope. These habits can be conquered, not only conquered temporarily, they can be rooted out completely. For that what is required is that Calm Inner Light of intuitive awakening — means that connection has to come which intuitively sees the future. “This habit is not going to help me in the long run.”. So that conviction has to come from inside so that it can be rooted out. The Calm Intuitive Awakening is represented by DHRISHTADYUMNA, who fought on behalf of PANDAVAS. And he’s the one, eventually, who killed DRONACHARYA, the habit. So, we also have to generate that awakening conviction inside — calm inner light of intuitive awakening. How? By spiritual practices. Because DHRISHTADYUMNA came out of fire after his father DRUPADA did intense SADHANA, intense TAPAS. Then he came out of fire to help him. Similarly, I have to do intense SADHANA, then that awakening comes inside, conviction. So, with that I can conquer my habits.
Next, we studied SLOKAS four, five and six. Here one basic principle to understand. The five PANDAVAS could not have won the war by themselves. They needed help, the help of many allies. Many kings came forward to help them, support them — like DRUPADA, VIRATA, KASHIRAJA, KUNTIBHOJA and the like. Similarly, my self-control and PRANAYAMA, YAMA-NIYAMA alone are not adequate to win this KURUKSHETRA within. I require the support of other spiritual qualities like devotion, spiritual memory, PRANAYAMA, and discriminative intelligence. And these things are the spiritual effects a devotee gathers by regular practice of yoga meditation — meaning one need not necessarily be born with the spiritual qualities like devotion and intelligence and spiritual memory, PRANAYAMA, etc. One can gather by the practice of regular meditation. So, as we practise spiritual SADHANA these qualities come up to our aid. They can be cultivated, even if we don’t have them in full strength, as we go along. And in SLOKAS seven and eight, PARAMAHANSA YOGANANDAJI points out the KAURAVAS about whom a devotee must be wary, wary, because they represent specific principles that oppose spiritual progress — like AVIDYA, illusion, ego, habit, attachment, repulsion, latent desire. These are there inside. We should be aware of their existence and conquer them. Like PANDAVAS had to face formidable, very strong opponents like BHISHMA, DRONA, KARNA, VIKARNA, ASHVATTHAMAN, like that, we also have to face.
